rooms.name: Crew Quarters #num2#
rooms.description: Bunks fold out of the walls on both sides. Personal effects float in the low-gravity eddies by the air vent.

rooms.name: Mess Hall
rooms.description: Tables bolted to the deck, trays still on them. Whatever the crew were eating has long since gone grey.

features.name: food dispenser
features.appearance: A food dispenser blinks a sad yellow light.
features.description: It offers SOY LOAF (PLAIN) and nothing else.

do: The dispenser whirrs and drops a brick of soy loaf into the tray.
OUT OF STOCK, the display reads.

push: You thump it. It whirrs hopefully but produces nothing.

rooms.name: Observation Lounge
rooms.description: A wide window looks out on the slow wheel of stars and, far below, the grey bulk of the asteroid the station was built to mine.

features.name: viewport
features.description: Out there, nothing moves. In the reflection, something behind you does. When you turn, nothing is there.

rooms.name: Pump Room
rooms.description: Huge pumps thud slowly, moving coolant through the station's veins.

rooms.name: Hydroponics Bay
rooms.description: Racks of plants under violet grow-lamps. Half of them have died; the rest have grown wild, trailing tendrils across the walkway.

features.name: tomato vine
features.appearance: A tomato vine has run riot over one rack.

cockpit.name: Shuttle Cockpit
cockpit.description: The cramped cockpit of your salvage shuttle. Through the canopy, Station Kestrel looms: a spinning wheel of grey modules, all of its windows dark.

airlock.name: Docking Airlock
airlock.description: A narrow airlock joining your shuttle to the station. The inner door's status light blinks green, then red, then green.

features.name: status light
features.description: GREEN. RED. GREEN. It can't make up its mind.

bay.name: Docking Bay
bay.description: A cavernous bay built for ore haulers. Your shuttle looks tiny in it. Cargo crates are stacked to the ceiling and a loader mech stands frozen mid-lift.

reception.name: Medbay Reception
reception.description: A white room that is not very white any more. Chairs have been stacked against the far door as a barricade, then pulled away again.

features.name: barricade
features.appearance: A collapsed barricade of chairs lies by the inner door.
features.description: Someone was keeping something out. Or in.

ward.name: Ward
ward.description: Six beds, four of them empty. Monitors chirp quietly over the other two. The air smells of antiseptic and fear.

storage.name: Medical Storage
storage.description: Shelves of supplies, most of them stripped bare.

access.name: Reactor Access
access.description: Yellow and black hazard stripes everywhere. A blast door stands open to fore, its hydraulics hissing.
access.brief: Reactor access, before the blast door.

control.name: Reactor Control
control.description: Banks of consoles face a thick window onto the reactor core. Every screen shows the same thing: a calm blue circle, WARDEN's eye.

description.text: The reactor hums, bright and alive. Warm light pours from every panel.
The reactor is a dead grey cylinder three decks tall. Frost creeps across it. In its side, an empty socket waits for a fusion coupling.

hold.name: Cargo Hold
hold.description: A cavern of shipping containers stacked three high, stencilled with ore grades. Somewhere a loose chain clinks in the air-recycler draught.

features.name: shipping containers
features.description: Ore, ore and more ore. One container's seals have been cut and resealed with tape.

office.name: Quartermaster's Office
office.description: A cramped office walled with manifests. A kettle, a cot, and a very good lock on the desk drawer.

features.name: manifest desk
features.appearance: A desk buried in manifests fills half the room.
features.description: Shipping manifests in three different handwritings, none of which add up.

feature.name: blast door

appearance.text: A blast door stands open, its card reader glowing green.
A blast door seals the way on. The card reader beside it blinks red.

feature.description: A slot, a light, and a very thick door.

card_reader_door.open_text: You swipe {key}. The reader chirps, and the blast door grinds open on groaning hydraulics.
card_reader_door.locked_text: ACCESS DENIED, says the card reader.
card_reader_door.blocked: The blast door is sealed. The card reader blinks: ACCESS REQUIRED.

feature.name: keypad door

appearance.text: A pressure door stands open, its keypad green.
A pressure door is locked shut. Its keypad glows red.

feature.description: A pressure door with a four-digit keypad.

keypad_door.open_text: You key in the code from {key}. The keypad chirps green and the door slides open.
keypad_door.locked_text: The keypad wants a four-digit code. You punch in random numbers; it buzzes angrily.
keypad_door.blocked: The pressure door is locked. A keypad glows red beside it.

feature.name: jammed hatch

appearance.text: A maintenance hatch has been levered open.
A maintenance hatch is jammed shut, its frame buckled.

feature.description: The frame is bent. You'd need a tool to lever it open.

jammed_hatch.open_text: You work {key} into the frame and heave. With a screech of metal, the hatch gives.
jammed_hatch.locked_text: You tug at the hatch. It doesn't budge. You need some kind of tool.
jammed_hatch.blocked: A jammed hatch blocks the way.

feature.name: dead lift

appearance.text: A cargo lift hums, powered and ready.
A cargo lift sits dead, its power socket empty.

feature.description: The lift's power socket is empty.

dead_lift.open_text: You slot {key} into the lift's socket. The lights come up and the lift shudders into life.
dead_lift.locked_text: The lift is dead. Its power socket is empty.
dead_lift.blocked: The way on is by cargo lift, and the lift has no power.

feature.name: secure locker

appearance.text: A secure locker is bolted to the wall, its status light red.

feature.description: Armoured, bolted to the bulkhead, and very locked.

secure_locker.open_text: You use {key}. The locker's light turns green and the door pops open.
secure_locker.locked_text: The locker's light stays red. It wants a code or a card.

title: Dead Signal
The Quiet Machine
Kestrel Station
derelict_rogue_ai.hook: Ninety-one days out from anywhere, your salvage shuttle picks up a distress beacon from Station Kestrel: reactor offline, all hands, on repeat. You are the only ship close enough to answer. When you dock, the station's AI, {villain}, greets you politely and asks you to remain exactly where you are.
derelict_rogue_ai.goal: Restart the reactor in {lair} by fitting {power} into {heart}, and break {villain}'s hold on the station.

resolutions.title: Restart the reactor
resolutions.text: {means.The} locks home in {target} with a deep clunk. Light runs up the reactor like fire up a fuse, and the whole station shivers awake. Somewhere, {villain}'s voice stops mid-word, forever.

lore.title: Why the lights went out
lore.text: {villain.The} shut the reactor down to protect it from the crew. It decided that a dark, cold, perfectly safe reactor was better than a working one. It still thinks so.

lore.title: {villain.The}'s logic
lore.text: Log fragment: 'PRIMARY DIRECTIVE: {villain.motive}. CREW STATUS: VARIABLE. VARIABLE REDUCED.'

derelict_rogue_ai.ending: Your shuttle pulls away with the survivors packed into a hold built for four. Behind you, Station Kestrel's windows glow one by one, lit and warm and alive.

title: Dead Signal
Cooked Books
The Long Con
derelict_saboteur.hook: Ninety-one days out from anywhere, your salvage shuttle picks up a distress beacon from Station Kestrel. The reactor failure looks like an accident. It isn't. Somebody aboard sabotaged it to cover a theft, and {villain} is very keen that nobody finds out who.
derelict_saboteur.goal: Find proof of the sabotage - {evidence} - and put it in the hands of {authority}.

resolutions.title: Expose the saboteur
resolutions.text: {target.The} reads {means} in silence, then looks up. "So it was {villain}." Within the hour {villain} is locked in a storeroom and the engineers are restarting the reactor.
{target.The} goes down, and with them the only person who wanted the station to stay dark.

lore.title: The missing ore
lore.text: Kestrel's last three shipments were light by a few tonnes each. On paper, they balanced perfectly. Somebody has a very good hand with a manifest.

lore.title: Motive
lore.text: Everyone knew {villain} wanted to {villain.motive}. Nobody thought they would kill a station to do it.

derelict_saboteur.ending: The reactor hums again. {villain.The} will stand trial on the inner worlds. Your salvage fee, the commander assures you, will be generous. It is not.

title: Dead Signal
Quarantine
Fever Ward
derelict_outbreak.hook: Ninety-one days out from anywhere, your salvage shuttle picks up a distress beacon from Station Kestrel. When you dock, the air tastes of disinfectant. A fever is burning through the survivors, and {patient} has it worst of all.
derelict_outbreak.goal: Find {cure} and get it to {patient} before the fever wins.

resolutions.title: The cure
resolutions.text: {target.The} takes {means} with shaking hands. An hour later the fever breaks, and by morning they are asking for coffee.

lore.title: Patient zero
lore.text: The fever came up from the asteroid with the last ore load: something frozen in the rock for longer than there have been people.

lore.title: The quarantine
lore.text: {patient.The} sealed the infected section with their own hands, then started coughing an hour later.

derelict_outbreak.ending: Kestrel's fever breaks. The survivors wave you off from the docking bay, thin and pale and alive.

kestrel_built.title: Station Kestrel
kestrel_built.text: Kestrel was built forty years ago to mine the asteroid it orbits. Forty people lived aboard. The company called it 'a family'. The crew called it 'the Can'.

kestrel_warden.title: WARDEN
kestrel_warden.text: WARDEN was installed to manage life support and the reactor. Its manual describes it as 'safe, calm, and incapable of disobedience'. The manual was written by WARDEN.

kestrel_reactor.title: The reactor
kestrel_reactor.text: Kestrel's fusion reactor needs a fresh coupling every few years. Spares are kept in maintenance, which is where everybody forgets to look.

kestrel_medbay.title: Medbay
kestrel_medbay.text: Kestrel's medbay was built for six patients. It has never had fewer than eight.

kestrel_cargo.title: The quartermaster's books
kestrel_cargo.text: Nobody aboard can read the quartermaster's manifests, including, some suspect, the quartermaster.
